# web-mojo admin extension — dnsman management pages

- **Kind**: feature
- **Date**: 2026-07-26
- **Requested by**: Ian (ian@nativemojo.com)
- **Depends on**: django-mojo **item 392** (dnsman) — *note: that item lives on board 8 / workspace 10 (Maestro) alongside #391, not on this board*. It is built and green; the REST surface below is live.
- **Backend capability dependency**: board **item 412** (django-mojo — batch TLD availability, domain suggestions, per-TLD price cache, config additions) — **DONE, shipped in v1.2.55** (2026-07-26). Exact shapes read from the shipped source are in the *Backend capability surface* section; the delivered `GET /api/dnsman/config` is richer than proposed and several fields improved the plan (provider matrix, ACME state, price cap, renewal window). Older backends degrade to an explanatory note, not a client-side reimplementation.

## Description

`mojo.apps.dnsman` shipped in django-mojo: a framework app for domain purchase,
DNS record management across Route53 **and** BYO GoDaddy accounts, WHOIS/privacy,
SES email records, and centrally-issued/custodied TLS certificates.

It has **no UI**. The web-mojo admin extension already ships ~50 `system/*` pages
covering django-mojo apps (Messaging, Storage, Shortlinks, Job engine, Push…), so
dnsman belongs there too — otherwise every consuming product rebuilds these
tables itself.

## Proposed pages (`system/dns/*`)

| Route | Content |
|---|---|
| `system/dns/domains` | Domain table — name, provider, status, expiry, auto-renew, privacy, group. Detail view with the DNS record editor. |
| `system/dns/records` | Live record editor for a selected domain (reads/writes the provider, not a DB mirror) |
| `system/dns/credentials` | `DnsCredential` table — link/rotate a provider key, verified state, last error. **Masked values only.** |
| `system/dns/purchases` | Purchase ledger — read-only; domain, price, our cost, status, operation id, error |
| `system/dns/certificates` | Certificate table — SANs, status, issuer, validity, `days_remaining`, `renew_after`; request/revoke actions |

Permissions follow the existing convention: `view_dns` renders read-only,
write controls additionally require `manage_dns` (or the `security` domain
category). Two surfaces are deliberately stricter on the backend and the UI must
respect that rather than offer a button that 403s:

- **Adopt** (`registrar/adopt`) is platform-**superuser** only.
- **Certificate material** requires `manage_dns`, not `view_dns` — and the UI
  should almost certainly not expose a "download private key" control at all;
  that endpoint exists for serving hosts syncing via the job channel.

## Notes for whoever scopes this

- **Purchase is a two-step flow by construction.** `registrar/quote` returns a
  price plus a single-use `confirm_token` that is shown **exactly once** and is
  never retrievable again (only its hash is stored). The UI must capture it from
  the quote response and present an explicit cost confirmation before calling
  `registrar/purchase`. There is deliberately no single-call purchase path.
- **Purchasing ships disabled** (`DNSMAN_PURCHASE_ENABLED` defaults False), so
  the pages must degrade gracefully rather than appear broken.
- **Availability is tri-state**: `true`, `false`, or **`null`** meaning the
  registry did not answer. Rendering `null` as "unavailable" would tell a user a
  buyable name is taken.
- **Record values are a list** — the API field is `record_values`, always an
  array even for one value (a wildcard and its apex legitimately share one TXT
  name with two values).
- Registration is **asynchronous** (minutes); a cron advances it. The purchase
  view needs to poll or refresh rather than assume a synchronous result.
- Provider differences are already hidden by the backend dispatch, but the UI
  should surface that GoDaddy-backed domains are **management-only** — purchase
  and WHOIS endpoints refuse them with an explicit message.

## Reference

- REST contract: `docs/web_developer/dnsman/README.md` in django-mojo (endpoints,
  request/response shapes, permissions, error shapes)
- Backend architecture: `docs/django_developer/dnsman/README.md`
- Existing admin conventions: `docs/web-mojo/extensions/Admin.md`, and
  `src/admin.js` as the single source of truth for the `(route, page, permissions)` mapping

## Out of scope

- Any purchase *policy* (spend caps, allowlists, credits) — that is product-level,
  not framework admin.
- Hosting / certificate installation on serving boxes.

---

## Plan

### Objective

Ship the `system/dns/*` admin surface in the web-mojo admin extension over the
live `/api/dnsman` REST contract: five registered pages, one sidebar group, the
`view_dns` / `manage_dns` permissions registered in the UI permission catalog,
and detail views for Domain, DnsCredential and Certificate. Every write control
is gated so it can never render for a caller the backend will refuse.

**Scope includes the buy-a-domain wizard** (`registrar/search` → `quote` →
confirm → `purchase`, plus provisioning poll), alongside the two free
onboarding paths (`registrar/register-existing`, `registrar/adopt`). Scoping
initially proposed deferring the wizard; Ian reversed that — without it the
surface only works on a deployment that already owns domains. See D1.

**Two scope additions from the design review (Ian, 2026-07-26):**

- **Multi-TLD / similar-name search** in the wizard's first step — a results
  grid rather than a single-name answer. Backed by the django-mojo endpoints
  from **board item 412** (shipped v1.2.55); an older backend gets the exact
  row plus an explanatory note. See D10.
- **A hardened DNS record editor** — structured per-type value editors, paste
  autofix, cross-record collision checks against the loaded zone, and a
  diff-before-save. Record editing is where people actually break production
  DNS, and the backend deliberately validates structure but not value syntax.
  See D9.

### Verified API surface (read from django-mojo source, not just the doc)

Endpoints (`/api/dnsman` prefix), all wrapped by mojo as
`{status: true, code: 200, data: <payload>}` — payload at `resp.data.data`:

| Endpoint | Method | Gate | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `domain`, `domain/<pk>` | GET/POST | VIEW / SAVE | `CAN_CREATE=False`. Writable: `auto_renew`, `privacy`, `credential`, `metadata` only |
| `dns?domain=<pk>` | GET | VIEW | `{domain, provider, records:[{type,name,record_values,ttl}]}` — live provider read, no ids |
| `dns` | POST | SAVE | upsert; `record_values` is the COMPLETE desired list |
| `dns/delete` | POST | SAVE | omit `record_values` to drop the whole set |
| `credential`, `credential/<pk>` | GET/POST | VIEW / SAVE | `CAN_CREATE=False`; masked-only (`api_key_masked`, `api_secret_masked`) |
| `credential/link` | POST | SAVE | create **and** rotate (pass `credential: <pk>`); verifies before persisting |
| `purchase`, `purchase/<pk>` | GET | VIEW | `CAN_CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE = False` — read-only ledger |
| `config` | GET | VIEW | capability object — see *Backend capability surface* (v1.2.55) |
| `registrar/search` | POST | VIEW | `{domain}` → flat row (tri-state `available`); `{domain, tlds}` / `{domains}` → `{results:[…]}` |
| `registrar/suggest` | POST | VIEW | `{domain, count, only_available}` → `{results:[…]}`, same row shape (v1.2.55) |
| `registrar/quote` | POST | SAVE | returns `{purchase, name, price, currency, years, token, expires, privacy_supported}` — `token` is raw, **shown exactly once**, only its SHA-256 is stored |
| `registrar/purchase` | POST | SAVE | returns `{purchase, domain, name, status, operation_id, privacy, privacy_downgraded}`; redeemable exactly once |
| `registrar/adopt` | POST | SAVE **+ `request.user.is_superuser`** | literal superuser attribute |
| `registrar/register-existing` | POST | SAVE (+ SAVE on the credential) | BYO claim |
| `whois` | **GET** | **SAVE** | ⚠ read gated on `manage_dns` — returns real registrant PII |
| `whois`, `whois/privacy` | POST | SAVE | Route53 only |
| `certificate`, `certificate/<pk>` | GET/POST | VIEW / SAVE | no PEM in any graph |
| `certificate/request`, `certificate/revoke` | POST | SAVE | issuance is a background job (minutes) |
| `certificate/material/<pk>` | GET | SAVE (+ superuser for house certs) | **not exposed in this UI** |

Model field names confirmed against the django-mojo `RestMeta.GRAPHS`:

- `Domain` — `id, created, modified, name, provider, status, hosted_zone_id, auto_renew, privacy, verified, registered_on, expires, last_error` + graphs `group`, `user`, `credential`. `status ∈ pending|registering|active` (`failed` rows are deleted, never persist).
- `DnsCredential` — `id, created, modified, name, provider, is_active, verified, verified_at, domain_count, last_error` + extras `api_key_masked`, `api_secret_masked` + graph `group`.
- `DomainPurchase` — `id, created, modified, domain_name, kind, status, price, cost, currency, years, quote_expires, operation_id, error` + graphs `group`, `user`. `status ∈ quoted|submitted|completed|failed|expired`. `confirm_token` is `NO_SHOW`.
- `Certificate` — `id, created, modified, common_name, sans, status, issuer, serial, not_before, not_after, renew_after, last_error, attempts` + extra `days_remaining` + graph `domain`. `status ∈ pending|issuing|active|failed|revoked`. Group-scoped through `domain__group`.
- Allowed record types default to `["A","AAAA","CNAME","TXT","MX","SRV","CAA","NS"]` (`DNSMAN_ALLOWED_RECORD_TYPES` is server-configurable, so the form must survive a server rejection).

### Design artifact — delivered with this plan

**`planning/mockups/dnsman/index.html`** — the approved-design reference, built
and verified in **both themes** during scoping, not deferred into the build.
Eight surfaces behind a switcher: Domains · DomainView (5 sections) · **Record
editor** (structured per-type fields, autofix notice, blocking errors with the
type-swap fix, diff-before-save, and the non-happy states) · Credentials ·
Certificates · Purchases · Buy wizard (all five steps, the multi-TLD results
grid with all four availability states, the terminal registered/failed pair, and
the purchasing-disabled panel). Amber dashed blocks are spec annotations, not
product UI — they carry the reasoning for each gate so the build session doesn't
have to re-derive it from this document.

Mockups belong to design, not construction: a review that can change the shape
of the work has to happen before the plan is final, otherwise the plan isn't.
The build implements this; it does not redesign it.

### Implementation steps

Four ordered commits. The design is settled (see above), so Commit A starts
immediately.

#### Commit A — data layer + permission registry

1. **`src/extensions/admin/models/Dns.js`** (new). Follows
   `src/extensions/admin/models/Email.js` / `IPSet.js` shape: `Model` +
   `Collection` pairs plus a `*Forms` config object and option constants.
   - `Domain` / `DomainList` — endpoint `/api/dnsman/domain`.
   - `DnsCredential` / `DnsCredentialList` — endpoint `/api/dnsman/credential`;
     static `DnsCredential.link({group, provider, api_key, api_secret, name, credential})`
     → `POST /api/dnsman/credential/link` (same call creates and rotates).
   - `DomainPurchase` / `DomainPurchaseList` — endpoint `/api/dnsman/purchase`.
   - `Certificate` / `CertificateList` — endpoint `/api/dnsman/certificate`;
     static `Certificate.request({domain, names})`, instance `revoke()`.
   - `DnsRecord` / `DnsRecordList` — `DnsRecordList` has endpoint
     `/api/dnsman/dns` and overrides `parse(response)` to read
     `response.data.data.records`, stash `{domain, provider}` into
     `this.meta`, and synthesize `id = dnsData.recordKey(record)` so
     `Collection.add()`'s dedupe and `TableView`'s per-row models work.
     `options.size` is irrelevant (no server paging) — construct with
     `params: {}` and `paginated: false` downstream.
     Instance helpers `upsert(domainId, rec)` / `remove(domainId, rec)`
     posting to `dns` / `dns/delete`.
   - `registrar` helper export: `search(name)`, `quote({group, domain, years})`,
     `purchase({group, purchase, confirm_token})`,
     `registerExisting({group, domain, credential})`,
     `adopt({group, domain, create_zone})`, and `capabilities()` if the
     django-mojo probe lands (see "Dependency" below).
   - `whois` helper export: `get(domainId)`, `update(domainId, contact)`,
     `setPrivacy(domainId, enabled)`.
   - Forms: `DomainForms.edit` (auto_renew / privacy switches),
     `DnsRecordForms.upsert` (type select, name, values textarea, ttl),
     `DnsCredentialForms.link` (group, provider, name, api_key, api_secret),
     `DomainForms.registerExisting`, `DomainForms.adopt`,
     `CertificateForms.request` (domain select, names tag input).
   - Constants: `DomainProviderOptions`, `DomainStatusOptions`,
     `CertificateStatusOptions`, `PurchaseStatusOptions`, `DNS_RECORD_TYPES`.

2. **`src/extensions/admin/dns/dnsData.js`** (new) — pure, unit-testable
   helpers, no DOM and no `rest`. Mirrors the `geofenceData.js` precedent.
   This module carries essentially all the correctness of the feature, which is
   why it is pure and why its tests land in this same commit.

   *General — capability-derived, not hardcoded (see the Backend capability
   surface section; every one of these takes the `config` object rather than
   baking in a constant the server owns):*
   - `providerLabel(provider)`
   - `isManagementOnly(domain, caps)` → looks up `caps.providers[]` and returns
     `purchase === false`. **Not** `provider !== 'route53'` — the server now
     publishes the matrix, so a third provider gaining purchase support needs no
     web-mojo change.
   - `requiresCredential(provider, caps)` → from the same `providers[]` entry.
   - `recordKey(record)` → stable synthetic id, `` `${type}|${name}` ``
   - `isSpentAcmeChallenge(record)` → TXT + name starts `_acme-challenge` +
     `record_values` is exactly `['retired']`
   - `certExpiryTone(daysRemaining, caps)` → thresholds derived from
     `caps.cert_renew_days` (danger past renewal, warning approaching it,
     success otherwise, `secondary` for `null`) instead of hardcoded 14/30 that
     would silently disagree with the server's renewal scan.
   - `availabilityState(searchResult)` → `'available' | 'taken' | 'unknown' |
     'unsupported'`. The tri-state guard lives here, in one tested function, so
     `available: null` can never be collapsed into "taken" by a template.
   - `exceedsPriceCap(row, caps)` → `price > caps.max_domain_price`. Lets the
     grid mark a row as over-cap **before** the user picks it, rather than
     letting `registrar/quote` 400 after two more clicks.

   *Record type model — the single source of truth for the editor (D9):*
   - `RECORD_SPECS` — per type, the ordered field list with its value kind and
     whether the set may hold multiple values:

     | Type | Fields | Multi |
     |---|---|---|
     | `A` | `ip` (ipv4) | yes |
     | `AAAA` | `ip` (ipv6) | yes |
     | `CNAME` | `target` (hostname) | **no — single value only** |
     | `MX` | `priority` (uint16, default 10), `target` (hostname) | yes |
     | `SRV` | `priority`, `weight` (uint16), `port`, `target` (hostname) | yes |
     | `CAA` | `flags` (uint8, default 0), `tag` (issue\|issuewild\|iodef), `value` | yes |
     | `TXT` | `text` | yes |
     | `NS` | `target` (hostname) | yes |

   - `parseRecordValue(type, wireString)` → structured object
   - `formatRecordValue(type, structured)` → wire string
     Round-trip invariant: `format(parse(v)) === v` for every well-formed
     value. That property is the test.

   *Autofix — `autofixRecordValue(type, raw)` → `{ value, fixes: [...] }`.*
   Never silent: every fix is returned so the UI can list what it changed.
   - trim; strip zero-width and non-breaking spaces
   - smart quotes (`" " ' '`) → ASCII
   - hostname-valued fields: strip `http(s)://`, any path, trailing `/`,
     trailing dot; lowercase
   - **TXT: strip user-added surrounding quotes.** Route53 quotes and
     255-chunks TXT itself (`providers/base.py` `TXT_TYPES`), so a pasted
     `"v=spf1 …"` becomes double-quoted and SPF/DKIM breaks **silently** — the
     backend's own docstring names this as a silent-breakage class.
   - A/AAAA: strip surrounding `[ ]`
   - a bare `10 mail.example.com` pasted into an MX target splits into
     priority + target
   - drop blanks, dedupe values

   *Blocking validation — `validateRecordSet({type, name, values, ttl, zone, existingRecords})`.*
   Mirrors the backend rules so the user never round-trips a 400, and adds the
   value-syntax checks the backend deliberately does not make:
   - *mirrored:* name inside zone, apex `NS`/`SOA` refused, DNS label charset,
     wildcard only as the leftmost label, type in `config.allowed_record_types`
     (falling back to the client default only on a backend without `config`)
   - IPv4 required in `A`, IPv6 in `AAAA` — and when the value is valid for the
     *other* type, offer a one-click "change type to AAAA" fix rather than an
     error the user has to interpret
   - `CNAME` at the apex → blocked
   - `CNAME` with more than one value → blocked
   - `CNAME` at a name that already holds any other record → blocked
   - any type at a name that already holds a `CNAME` → blocked
     (both collision checks are possible because the whole zone is already
     loaded in the view — no extra request)
   - `MX`/`SRV`/`NS`/`CNAME` targets must be hostnames, not IPs
   - `CAA` tag ∈ {`issue`, `issuewild`, `iodef`}
   - numeric ranges: priority/weight uint16, port 1–65535, flags uint8
   - TTL 60–86400

   *Non-blocking warnings — `recordWarnings(...)`, confirm-to-proceed:*
   - editing or deleting a **live** `_acme-challenge` TXT (i.e. not the spent
     `['retired']` form) — an in-flight issuance can fail
   - replacing/removing the apex or `www` `A`/`AAAA` — takes the site offline
   - any `MX` change — changes mail delivery
   - TTL below 300
   - creating a wildcard record
   - `SRV` name that isn't `_service._proto.name`

   *Diff — `diffRecordValues(before, after)` → `{ added, removed, unchanged }`.*
   The single most valuable control on the surface, because an upsert
   **replaces the whole set**. Any save that removes values shows the diff
   first, naming each value that will disappear.

3. **`src/core/models/User.js`** — register the permissions so an admin can
   actually grant them:
   - Platform tab (`User.GRANULAR_PERMISSION_TABS`) += `view_dns` ("View DNS"),
     `manage_dns` ("Manage DNS", tooltip noting adopt and certificate material
     stay superuser-only).
   - `User.CATEGORY_GRANULAR_MAP.security` += `"view_dns", "manage_dns"` —
     exactly mirrors the backend, whose `VIEW_PERMS`/`SAVE_PERMS` both accept
     the `security` category.
   - Deliberately **no** `Member.BASE_PERMISSIONS` entry (see D4).

4. Run `npm run generate:models` → regenerates
   `src/extensions/admin/models/index.js` (commit it; `.claude/rules/git.md`).

5. **Unit tests for everything in this commit** — `DnsData`,
   `DnsRecordValidation`, `DnsRecordList` (detailed under Testing plan). The
   pure logic is tested where it lands, not deferred to a trailing commit.

#### Commit B — pages and wiring

6. **`src/extensions/admin/dns/DnsRecordsView.js`** — the reusable record
   editor, `model` = the Domain. Built hardened from the start; it is a thin
   shell over the `dnsData` functions from Commit A.

   *Table.* One `TableView` over a `DnsRecordList` with
   `paginated:false, searchable:false, filterable:false` (the endpoint has no
   server search/paging); a type filter is applied client-side by holding the
   full array on the view and calling `collection.reset(filtered)`.
   Columns: Type (badge), Name, Values (escaped, one per line, truncated), TTL,
   row actions Edit / Delete gated on `manage_dns`.
   Toolbar: Add record (`manage_dns`), Refresh.

   *Editor (D9).* The value input is **structured per record type**, driven by
   `RECORD_SPECS` — MX renders (priority, target) rows, SRV four fields, CAA
   (flags, tag, value), A/AAAA validated IP rows, CNAME a single hostname with
   the add-row control suppressed. Changing the type rebuilds the fields and
   attempts to carry the values across via `parse`/`format`. Existing records
   load through `parseRecordValue`, so editing an MX never means hand-editing
   `"10 mail.example.com"` as a string.

   *Autofix.* Runs on paste and blur; the applied fixes render as a short
   "we changed this" list above the fields, never silently.

   *Validation.* `validateRecordSet` on every change — blocking errors disable
   Save and attach to the offending field; the IPv4-in-AAAA case offers the
   one-click type swap. Collisions are checked against the loaded zone, so a
   CNAME clash is caught before the request.

   *Save.* When the change removes any value, a diff confirm
   (`diffRecordValues`) lists exactly what disappears — this is the guard
   against the whole-set-replace footgun. Warnings from `recordWarnings` appear
   in the same confirm and require an explicit proceed.

   *States.* Domain not `active` → explanatory panel instead of the table (the
   backend's `_require_active` refuses); fetch error → render the server
   message verbatim; spent `_acme-challenge` rows muted with a tooltip.

   *Server is still the authority.* Every client check mirrors a backend rule
   or adds a syntax check the backend leaves open — none of it replaces the
   server's validation, and a server rejection is always surfaced verbatim.

7. **`src/extensions/admin/dns/DomainView.js`** (`DetailView`) — header
   `bi-globe2`, `titleField: 'name'`, chips for provider / status (function
   variant) / verified / expiring-soon, no active toggle (`status` is
   server-owned). Sections:
   - `Overview` — read-only facts plus an autosaving `FormView`
     (`autosaveModelField: true`) for `auto_renew` + `privacy`; the privacy
     switch is disabled with an inline reason on a management-only domain.
   - `Records` — `DnsRecordsView`.
   - `WHOIS` — `permissions: ['manage_dns']` (SideNavView gating, fail-closed);
     hidden with a management-only note for non-Route53.
   - `Certificates` — `CertificateList` scoped `?domain=<id>` with
     `hideActivePillNames` so the scoping pill can't be removed.
   - `Purchases` — `DomainPurchaseList` scoped by `domain_name`, read-only.
   Kebab: *Request certificate* (`manage_dns`), *Delete domain* (danger,
   `manage_dns`) — confirm copy must say this removes our record, **not** the
   registration.

8. **`src/extensions/admin/dns/DomainTablePage.js`** (`TablePage`) — columns
   name / provider / status / group / expires / auto-renew / privacy / verified.
   `showAdd: false` (`CAN_CREATE=False`); onboarding lives in `toolbarButtons`:

   Status filter omits `failed` (never persists) with a code comment saying why.

9. **`src/extensions/admin/dns/DnsRecordsPage.js`** (`Page`, route
   `system/dns/records`) — domain picker (active domains) above a
   `DnsRecordsView`; honours `?domain=<id>` so DomainView can deep-link.
   Fetch in `onEnter()` fire-and-forget with the stash + `onAfterMount` apply,
   per the WM-023 page-lifecycle rule.

10. **`src/extensions/admin/dns/DnsCredentialTablePage.js` + `DnsCredentialView.js`**
    — table: name / provider / verified / active / domain_count / last_error /
    created. Add → the link form → `credential/link`; on failure surface the
    verification error verbatim. DetailView: masked key/secret, `verified_at`,
    `domain_count`, `last_error`; header `activeField: 'is_active'`; kebab
    *Rotate key* (re-uses the link form with `credential: id`) and *Delete*.
    **No reveal control** — the secret is never returned by any endpoint.

11. **`src/extensions/admin/dns/CertificateTablePage.js` + `CertificateView.js`**
    — table: common_name / status / SAN count / issuer / not_after /
    days_remaining (toned via `certExpiryTone`) / domain. Toolbar *Request
    certificate* (`manage_dns`); row *Revoke* (danger, `manage_dns`,
    `when: status === 'active'`). Non-terminal rows (`pending`/`issuing`)
    drive the opt-in `autoRefresh` (WM-038) — idempotent-start,
    self-terminating tick, per the WM-034 cached-page-unmount seam.
    DetailView sections Overview / SANs / Renewal, plus a short note that key
    material is delivered to serving hosts over the job channel.
    **No download/material control anywhere** (D6).

    *Two capability-driven states the shipped `config` makes possible:*
    - `acme.configured === false` → *Request certificate* is disabled with
      "ACME isn't configured on this deployment", instead of a request that
      fails for a reason the operator can't see.
    - `acme.staging === true` → a **persistent warning banner** on the page:
      certificates issued against the Let's Encrypt staging directory are
      **not publicly trusted**. Silently shipping a staging cert to a
      production host is the kind of thing that costs an afternoon; the
      backend publishes the flag precisely so a UI can say so.

12. **`src/extensions/admin/dns/DomainPurchaseTablePage.js`** — read-only:
    `showAdd:false`, no edit/delete row actions. Columns created / domain_name /
    kind / status / price+currency / cost / years. `rowExpand` (WM-038) reveals
    `operation_id`, `quote_expires` and `error` — no DetailView needed (D7).

13. **`src/admin.js`** — exports + `registerSystemPages()` entries for the five
    routes, each `{permissions: ["view_dns", "manage_dns"]}`, and a new sidebar
    group placed after **Storage**:
    `DNS` (`bi-globe2`) → Domains (`bi-globe`), DNS Records (`bi-list-columns`),
    Certificates (`bi-patch-check`), Credentials (`bi-key`), Purchases (`bi-receipt`).

14. **`src/extensions/admin/css/admin.css`** — the structured record editor
    needs rules the Bootstrap utilities can't carry (the per-type field grid,
    the autofix notice, the diff list). Any literal surface colour owes a
    `[data-bs-theme="dark"]` companion clustered at the bottom of the file
    (`.claude/rules/theming.md`).

15. **`test/unit/DnsViews.test.js`** — view construction/config tests (below).

#### Commit C — buy-a-domain wizard

Sequenced last on purpose (D1): it lands on top of a surface already verified
green, so registrar iteration can't destabilize the rest.

16. **`src/extensions/admin/dns/DomainPurchaseWizard.js`** (new) — a stepped
    `View` shown in a modal, opened from the Domains toolbar's *Buy a domain*
    button (`manage_dns`). Five steps, each a distinct render state on **one**
    view so the shown-once token never crosses a component boundary:

   1. **Search — a results grid, not one answer (D10).**

      **A typed TLD never collapses the grid.** `nativemojo.com` and
      `nativemojo` produce the same three-part result; the only difference is
      that the first form pins an exact-match row:

      1. **The exact name typed**, pinned at the top and labelled as the one
         you asked for (only when a TLD was given).
      2. The bare label across the default TLD set.
      3. Similar-name suggestions.

      This is deliberate. `.com` is the likeliest name to be taken, so
      answering a full-name search with a single "already registered" row is
      exactly the dead end this feature exists to remove — the alternatives
      have to be on screen at the moment the bad news is.

      *Ordering guarantee:* `search_batch` returns rows **in request order**,
      so sending the exact name first means it is row 1 of the response — no
      client-side sorting, and the section split is a slice.

      *Data source (item 412 has landed — v1.2.55):*
      - `POST registrar/search` `{domain, tlds:[…]}` → `{results:[…]}` for the
        exact row + TLD grid in one call, and `POST registrar/suggest`
        `{domain}` → `{results:[…]}` for the similar-names block. Both return
        the identical row shape, so one renderer covers all three sections.
      - The TLD list sent is bounded by `search_batch_limit` from `config`
        (default 10) — never send more than the server will accept; over the
        cap it 400s naming the limit.
      - **Older backend** (no `suggestions_enabled` in config, or a batch
        response with no `results` key): render only the exact-name row via
        plain single-name `registrar/search`, plus a note that TLD comparison
        needs django-mojo ≥ v1.2.55. No client-side fan-out (D10).
      - A `registrar/suggest` failure (most likely the missing
        `route53domains:GetDomainSuggestions` IAM grant on first deploy) renders
        the block as "unavailable right now" with the server's message — not as
        an empty result, which would read as "no similar names exist".

      *Every row* renders through `dnsData.availabilityState()`, never raw
      `available`: `available` → price + Select; `taken` → "already
      registered" (with a pointer to *Register existing* if they hold it);
      `unknown` (`available: null`) → "the registry hasn't answered" + per-row
      Retry, and **never** the word unavailable; `unsupported`
      (`tld_supported: false`) → not sold here. The backend returns a `reason`
      string for every non-happy case — render it verbatim rather than
      composing our own. A row that errors or times out is `unknown`, not
      `taken`.

      Selecting a row carries that exact name into step 2.
   2. **Quote** — group + years → `POST registrar/quote`. The raw `token` is
      held in wizard instance state **only**: never localStorage, never a URL,
      never a log line, never re-fetchable. It dies with the view, and the view
      says so. Render `expires` as a live countdown (short TTL). A 400 naming
      `DNSMAN_PURCHASE_ENABLED` renders the kill-switch explanation, not a
      generic failure.
   3. **Confirm** — explicit cost confirmation before any money moves: name,
      years, price + currency, and — when `privacy_supported` is false — a
      plain statement that this TLD will not offer WHOIS privacy. A deliberate
      confirm affordance, not a bare OK.
   4. **Purchase** — `POST registrar/purchase {group, purchase, confirm_token}`.
      The button disables on first click and **never auto-retries**: a quote
      redeems exactly once and a second attempt returns a uniform 400 that
      deliberately does not say which check failed, so a retry could only
      mislead.
   5. **Provisioning** — registration is asynchronous (minutes). Poll
      `GET /api/dnsman/purchase/<pk>` with backoff until
      `completed` / `failed` / `expired`, using a self-terminating tick
      (WM-034: cached-page `unmount()` does not fire child `onBeforeUnmount`).
      `privacy_downgraded: true` → say the TLD refused privacy and it
      registered without it. On failure, show the ledger error and note the
      name is free to retry — the Domain row is deleted, so nothing blocks it.
      The modal stays closable throughout; the ledger and the domains table
      carry the state independently.

   **Pre-gating.** If the django-mojo capability probe lands (see Dependency),
   the *Buy a domain* control is hidden/disabled up front when purchasing is
   off. Without it the wizard degrades at step 2 instead — correct either way,
   but the probe is the difference between not offering the button and offering
   one that explains itself after two clicks.

17. **`src/extensions/admin/dns/DomainTablePage.js`** — add the *Buy a domain*
    toolbar button (`manage_dns`, plus the capability pre-gate if available).

#### Commit D — docs and release

19. Docs (below), `CHANGELOG.md`, `memory.md`, version bump. No test work left
    here by design — each commit ships its own.

### Design decisions

**D1 — The buy-a-domain wizard ships in this item.** Scoping first proposed
deferring it (only money path, disabled by default, carries the token /
tri-state / polling burden). Ian reversed that, correctly: without it the
surface can only manage domains the deployment *already* owns — `adopt` needs an
existing house hosted zone and `register-existing` needs a domain already held
at a provider. On a fresh deployment that owns nothing, every page renders
empty and there is no path out of that state from inside the admin. Buying is
the front door, so it ships with the rest.

The wizard is nonetheless the riskiest piece, so it is sequenced **last**
(Commit C) behind a working, verified read/manage surface — a green Commit B is
the fallback if registrar behaviour forces iteration.

**D2 — One `DnsRecordsView`, two mounts.** The workspec lists both a records
editor inside the Domain detail view and a standalone `system/dns/records` page.
Building the editor twice would guarantee drift, so it is one View parameterized
by `model` (the Domain), mounted as a DomainView section and again under a
domain picker on the standalone page.

**D3 — `DnsRecordList` is a real `Collection` with an overridden `parse()`.**
The records endpoint returns an id-less array inside a non-standard envelope,
but `Collection.parse()` is an explicit override point and `_performFetch`
routes through it. Synthesizing `id` from `type|name` gets `TableView` — rows,
row actions, per-row re-render — for free. Filtering is client-side because
there is no server-side search or paging on this endpoint.

**D4 — DNS permissions register on `User`, not `Member`.** `view_dns` /
`manage_dns` go in the Platform tab of `User.GRANULAR_PERMISSION_TABS` and into
`CATEGORY_GRANULAR_MAP.security`, which mirrors the backend exactly (both
`VIEW_PERMS` and `SAVE_PERMS` accept `security`). `Member.BASE_PERMISSIONS` stays
the lean framework list — the same call WM-029 made for the geofence perms.

**D5 — The WHOIS section is gated on `manage_dns`, not `view_dns`.** Scoping
found a third stricter-than-documented surface the workspec did not list:
`GET /api/dnsman/whois` is gated on `SAVE_PERMS` because the registrar returns
the real registrant name, address, phone and email regardless of WHOIS privacy.
A `view_dns`-only operator must not see that section at all.

**D6 — No certificate-material control, at any permission level.** Matches the
workspec's instinct and the backend's intent: that endpoint exists for serving
hosts pulling with their own API key after a `certificate_updated` broadcast.
The CertificateView says so in a sentence instead.

**D7 — Purchases uses `rowExpand`, not a DetailView.** The ledger is read-only
with no actions; a detail modal would be an empty frame around four fields.

**D8 — Adopt is gated on `activeUser.get('is_superuser')`, not
`hasPermission('admin')`.** The backend checks the literal `is_superuser`
attribute. `hasPermission('admin')` is broader (the system-wide wildcard grant),
so gating on it would render a button that 403s for an `admin`-permissioned
non-superuser — exactly the failure the workspec asks us to avoid.

**D9 — The record editor is structured per type, not a free-text box.** Ian's
call, and the backend's own boundaries justify it: `services/dns.py` and
`naming.py` validate *structure* thoroughly — zone containment (including the
`www.attacker.com` re-suffix trap), apex NS/SOA, DNS label charset, wildcard
position, TXT quoting per provider — but nothing anywhere checks that an `A`
holds IPv4, that `MX` has a priority, that `SRV` has four fields, or that a
`CNAME` isn't colliding. A single "values" textarea makes the user assemble
`"10 mail.example.com"` and `"0 issue \"letsencrypt.org\""` by hand, which is
precisely where people break production DNS.

Three things make this worth the extra work rather than gold-plating:
- **Per-type fields delete an entire error class.** You cannot get the field
  count wrong when the form has the right number of fields.
- **The TXT quoting autofix prevents a *silent* failure.** Route53 quotes and
  chunks TXT itself; a pasted `"v=spf1 …"` gets double-quoted and SPF/DKIM
  breaks with no error anywhere — the backend docstring calls this out by name.
- **The diff-before-save covers the whole-set-replace semantic.** Both
  providers replace the entire record set on write, so a user editing one value
  of a three-value set can silently destroy the other two. Nothing but an
  explicit before/after prevents that.

All of it lives in pure functions in `dnsData.js` and is unit-tested there. The
view is a shell. The server remains the authority — every client rule mirrors a
backend rule or adds a syntax check the backend leaves open, and a server
rejection is always surfaced verbatim.

**D10 — Multi-TLD search goes through the real API; no client fan-out.**
Reading the backend settled it: `check_availability()` makes **two** AWS calls
per name (`check_domain_availability` plus an *uncached* `list_prices(tld)`), so
an 8-TLD grid from the browser is 16 AWS calls, half re-fetching static per-TLD
pricing. Worse, `CheckDomainAvailability` is the call that degrades to
`PENDING`/`DONT_KNOW` under load — the `available: null` state — so fanning out
increases the frequency of the one answer we cannot usefully show. And
similar-name suggestions were unbuildable client-side at all: AWS
`GetDomainSuggestions` returns them in one call and had no wrapper.

**django-mojo item 412 shipped it** (v1.2.55): batch search, suggest, a per-TLD
price cache, and the config additions. #394 consumes it directly.

*Revised fallback.* The earlier draft had a capped client fan-out for backends
without 412. That is now dead weight, and it was the wrong shape anyway —
web-mojo ships to consumers on varying django-mojo versions, and the house
precedent for a missing backend capability is an explanatory panel, not a
client-side reimplementation (`GeofencingPage` does exactly this for
pre-v1.2.42). So on a backend without batch search the grid renders **only the
exact-name row** — plain single-name `registrar/search`, which has always
existed and is unchanged — plus a note that TLD comparison and suggestions need
django-mojo ≥ v1.2.55. Less code, no pretending.

Detection is cheap and doubly safe: `suggestions_enabled` in `config`, and the
absence of a `results` key in a batch response (an older backend ignores `tlds`
and answers with the flat single row).

### Edge cases and error handling

1. `record_values` is always a list, and an upsert **replaces the whole set** —
   the editor is a repeatable-value form and the diff-before-save (22–30) makes
   the replacement explicit.
2. Spent `_acme-challenge` TXT on GoDaddy (`['retired']`) is inert, not a live
   challenge — rendered muted with an explanatory tooltip, never as an error.
3. GoDaddy cannot delete the last record of a type — surface the server's
   explicit refusal verbatim; do not pre-empt it with a client-side guess.
4. Management-only (non-Route53) domains: WHOIS and registrar surfaces are
   hidden with a stated reason rather than shown and refused.
5. Domain not `active` → the records endpoint refuses; render an explanatory
   panel, not an empty table.
6. Domain `status: failed` never persists (failures delete the row) — omitted
   from the status filter, with a comment.
7. Deleting a Domain removes our management record, **not** the registration —
   the confirm copy must say that.
8. `days_remaining` is `null` when `not_after` is unset → `secondary` tone, "—".
9. A purchase row can outlive its domain (failed registration deletes the
   Domain, keeps the ledger row) — the ledger must render standalone.
10. Credential secrets are never returned in any response; masked-only display,
    rotation is the only "change" path.
11. Group scoping: `?group=` narrows only. Context-scoped child lists inside
    DomainView set `hideActivePillNames` so the scoping filter can't be dropped.
12. Errors are a uniform `403`/`400` with no detail by design — render the
    server's message; never synthesize a reason.
13. Empty arrays (`sans: []`, `records: []`) — use the guarded piped-section
    forms; WM-023 is the cautionary tale.
14. Every dev- or server-supplied string reaching template HTML goes through
    `this.escapeHtml` (WM-020/WM-031); function formatters emit raw innerHTML.

Wizard-specific:

15. `available: null` means the registry did not answer — routed through
    `availabilityState()` to its own "unknown, retry" state. It must never
    render as taken; telling a user a buyable name is gone is the worst failure
    this surface can produce.
16. The `confirm_token` is shown once and never retrievable. Instance state
    only; if the modal is closed before confirming, the quote is simply lost
    and a new one must be taken. The UI says that before it matters.
17. A quote redeems exactly once. Confirm disables on click, never auto-retries,
    and the uniform 400 on a second attempt is rendered as-is — it deliberately
    does not say which check failed, and we must not guess on its behalf.
18. Registration is asynchronous; a failure deletes the Domain row but keeps the
    purchase row and its error, so the name stays retryable. The poll must
    terminate on `completed` / `failed` / `expired` and on view destruction.
19. `privacy_downgraded: true` — the TLD refused WHOIS privacy and the domain
    registered without it. Stated plainly; the domain row already reflects it.
20. Purchasing disabled (`DNSMAN_PURCHASE_ENABLED`) — pre-gated when the
    capability probe exists, otherwise an explicit kill-switch message at the
    quote step. Never a generic failure.
21. Multi-TLD grid: a row that errors, times out, or is throttled is `unknown`,
    **not** `taken`. Partial results render as they resolve rather than blocking
    on the slowest row.

Record-editor specific (D9):

22. `CNAME` cannot coexist with any other record at the same name, and cannot
    sit at the apex — both are checked client-side against the already-loaded
    zone, so the user is stopped before the request rather than by a 400.
23. `CNAME` sets are single-valued; the editor suppresses the add-row control
    rather than letting the user build a set the provider will reject.
24. IPv6 pasted into `A` (or IPv4 into `AAAA`) offers a one-click type swap —
    the value is right, the type is wrong, and an error message alone makes the
    user do the reasoning.
25. TXT values must NOT carry user-added surrounding quotes; the autofix strips
    them. Route53 re-quotes and 255-chunks, so double-quoting breaks SPF/DKIM
    and ACME validation **with no error surfaced anywhere**.
26. Hostname-valued fields (`CNAME`/`MX`/`SRV`/`NS` targets) reject IP
    addresses and autofix pasted `http(s)://`, paths and trailing dots.
27. Editing or deleting a **live** `_acme-challenge` TXT warns that an in-flight
    certificate issuance may fail. The spent `['retired']` form does not warn —
    it is inert (see 2).
28. Removing the last `A`/`AAAA` at the apex or `www`, or changing `MX`, warns
    before saving: these are the "site went down" / "mail stopped" cases.
29. TTL is bounded 60–86400 with a warning below 300. A single TXT value over
    255 chars is informational only — chunking is the provider's job.
30. The type select is built from `config.allowed_record_types`, falling back
    to the client default only on a backend without `GET /api/dnsman/config` —
    `DNSMAN_ALLOWED_RECORD_TYPES` is server-configurable and a hardcoded client
    copy silently drifts.

### Testing plan

Baseline first: `npm test` (full custom runner) **before the first edit**, result
recorded on the item's activity trail (`.claude/rules/build-baseline.md`).
`npm run lint` baseline is 0 errors / 316 warnings.

Tests ship **in the commit that introduces the code**, not in a trailing
commit — the pure logic in Commit A is where nearly all the risk lives, so it is
tested the moment it exists.

New suites:

- **`test/unit/DnsData.test.js`** *(Commit A)* — the general helpers:
  `recordKey` stability, `isSpentAcmeChallenge` (true only for the exact
  `['retired']` single-value case; false for a live challenge and for a
  two-value set), and `availabilityState` over all four search shapes.
  Capability-derived helpers get both paths: `isManagementOnly` /
  `requiresCredential` read `providers[]` and fall back sanely when `config`
  is the permissive default (old backend); `certExpiryTone` moves its
  thresholds with `cert_renew_days`; `exceedsPriceCap` handles
  `max_domain_price` arriving as a **string** (the backend sends
  `str(Decimal)`) and a `null`/absent price.
- **`test/unit/DnsRecordValidation.test.js`** *(Commit A)* — the record editor's
  correctness, and the largest suite in the item:
  - **Round-trip**: `formatRecordValue(type, parseRecordValue(type, v)) === v`
    for a table of well-formed values across all eight types — the property
    that keeps the structured editor honest.
  - **Autofix**: smart quotes, zero-width/NBSP, `https://` + path on a CNAME
    target, `[::1]` brackets, trailing dots, blank/duplicate values, a bare
    `10 mail.example.com` splitting into MX priority+target — and each case
    asserts the returned `fixes` list, since a silent autofix is a bug.
  - **TXT quoting**: a value the user wrapped in quotes comes back unwrapped;
    a value containing legitimate inner quotes is left alone. This test exists
    because the failure mode is silent.
  - **Blocking rules**: IPv4-in-`AAAA` and IPv6-in-`A` (and that the swap
    suggestion names the right target type); `CNAME` at apex; `CNAME` with two
    values; `CNAME` colliding with an existing record at that name; a new `A`
    at a name that already holds a `CNAME`; apex `NS`/`SOA`; out-of-zone names;
    bad wildcard position; IP in a hostname field; bad `CAA` tag; numeric
    ranges; TTL bounds.
  - **Warnings, and that they do NOT block**: live vs. spent
    `_acme-challenge`, apex/`www` address removal, `MX` change, low TTL,
    wildcard creation.
  - **`diffRecordValues`**: added/removed/unchanged, including the
    three-values-to-one shrink that the confirm dialog exists to catch.
- **`test/unit/DnsRecordList.test.js`** *(Commit A)* — `parse()` against the real
  mojo envelope `{status:true, code:200, data:{domain, provider, records:[…]}}`:
  models get synthetic ids; a single-value `record_values` stays a one-element
  array; `records: []` yields an empty collection (not one junk model);
  `this.meta` captures `provider`.
- **`test/unit/DnsViews.test.js`** *(Commit B)* — construction-only assertions
  per WM-026 (read `headerConfig` / `sectionsConfig`, drive handlers directly;
  no `render()`): the DomainView WHOIS section carries
  `permissions: ['manage_dns']`; no CertificateView section or menu item
  references certificate material; the Revoke item's `when` predicate is true
  only for `status === 'active'`; the record editor's save path refuses to
  submit while `validateRecordSet` reports an error.
- **`test/unit/DomainPurchaseWizard.test.js`** *(Commit C)* — driven through
  handlers rather than `render()` (WM-026):
  each of the four search shapes routes to the right row state, and
  **`available: null` never reaches the taken branch**; a batch row carrying a
  per-name `reason` (the backend's failure-isolation shape) resolves to
  `unknown`, not `taken`; `nativemojo.com` and `nativemojo` produce the same
  three sections with only the pinned row differing; the TLD list sent never
  exceeds `search_batch_limit`; an old-backend response with no `results` key
  falls back to the single exact row plus the version note and never throws; a
  `suggest` failure renders "unavailable", not empty; the raw `token` is
  reachable only from wizard
  instance state — never written to `localStorage`, a URL, or the model; the
  confirm handler is idempotent (a second invocation while the first is in
  flight does not re-POST); a purchase 400 renders the failure state and does
  **not** schedule a retry; the provisioning poll terminates on each of
  `completed` / `failed` / `expired` and stops when the view is destroyed.
- **`test/utils/simple-module-loader.js`** — register the new views and add
  `models/Dns.js` → the classes the views construct, per the WM-026 named-import
  trap (an unmapped named import resolves to `undefined` and throws at
  construction).

Then `npm test` again; the only acceptable end state is the recorded baseline
and nothing new. Finally a Chrome UI pass against a django-mojo carrying dnsman:
each page in **light and dark**, per `.claude/rules/theming.md` — real clicks via
`find` + `computer left_click`, never `.click()` through `javascript_tool`.

### Backend capability surface — item 412 has LANDED (django-mojo v1.2.55)

Board item **412** closed 2026-07-26 (6 commits, `c12a7c40`…`ba69c86f`). Shapes
below are read from the shipped source, not from the proposal — the delivered
config is **richer** than what was asked for, and several fields change the
plan for the better.

**Row shape — identical for single search, batch rows and suggest rows**
(`registrar._search_row`), so one grid renders all three:

```
{ name, available, status, price, currency, tld,
  tld_supported, privacy_supported, reason }
```

**Endpoints:**

| Call | Body | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `POST registrar/search` | `{domain}` | the flat row — **unchanged**, byte-identical to before |
| `POST registrar/search` | `{domain, tlds:[…]}` | `{results:[row,…]}` in request order |
| `POST registrar/search` | `{domains:[…]}` | `{results:[row,…]}` |
| `POST registrar/suggest` | `{domain, count=10, only_available=true}` | `{results:[row,…]}`, `count` clamped to 25 |
| `GET config` | — | the capability object below |

Refusals to respect client-side: mixing `tlds` and `domains` → 400; a deduped
list longer than `search_batch_limit` → 400 naming the limit. Per-name failures
are **isolated** — a bad name becomes its own row with `available: null` and a
`reason`, and the batch still returns 200.

**`GET /api/dnsman/config`** (`view_dns`) — the delivered fields:

| Field | What #394 does with it |
|---|---|
| `purchase_enabled` | pre-gate *Buy a domain* |
| `registrant_contact_configured` | pre-warn: purchasing will fail at quote without it |
| `max_domain_price`, `currency` | **pre-warn on a row priced over the cap**, instead of a 400 at quote |
| `quote_ttl_minutes` | seeds the step-2 countdown |
| `allowed_record_types` | builds the record editor's type select |
| `search_batch_limit` | bounds the TLD grid — never send more than the server accepts |
| `suggestions_enabled` | presence-detects batch search + suggest |
| `providers[]` `{name, purchase, requires_credential}` | **replaces the hardcoded `provider !== 'route53'`** in `isManagementOnly`, and drives the credential-required gate |
| `acme` `{configured, staging}` | Certificates page states ACME isn't configured rather than letting Request fail; **warns loudly when `staging` — staging certificates are not publicly trusted** |
| `cert_renew_days` | drives `certExpiryTone` thresholds instead of hardcoded 14/30 |

**Consequences for the plan (all folded in above):**

- `dnsData` derives from capabilities rather than hardcoding: `isManagementOnly`
  reads `providers[]`, `certExpiryTone` takes `cert_renew_days`.
- The wizard's fan-out fallback is **dropped** (D10 revised). It was written for
  a backend that no longer needs it, and web-mojo ships to consumers on older
  django-mojo, so the honest fallback is the house precedent: render the
  exact-name row (plain single search, always works) plus an explanatory note
  that TLD comparison and suggestions need django-mojo ≥ v1.2.55 — exactly what
  `GefencingPage` does for pre-v1.2.42 backends. Less code, and it never
  pretends to a capability the server lacks.
- One capability fetch per app session in `registrar.capabilities()`
  (`models/Dns.js`), cached on the module, permissive defaults on 404 so an old
  backend degrades rather than blanks.

**Operational note carried from 412's close:** `registrar/suggest` needs the
`route53domains:GetDomainSuggestions` IAM grant. A missing grant surfaces as a
clean retry message (the backend deliberately never echoes botocore text), so
the suggestions block must treat an error as "unavailable right now", not empty.

### Follow-up items to file

- None outstanding — the django-mojo work landed as item 412.
